meaning_fixes.before: There's no way it can reach him anymore.
meaning_fixes.after: There's no way it can reach them anymore.
meaning_fixes.reason: The referent is the same unnamed 'あの人' ('that person') from dialogue_10523, which the same translator correctly rendered gender-neutral one line earlier. 'him' asserts a gender the source does not give for this line and was inconsistent with the batch's own neutral treatment of the same referent; made neutral for consistency (BASE_RULES: do not infer/assume gender for an unidentified person).

meaning_fixes.before: Did we just enter the Zone?!
meaning_fixes.reason: 'just' is not present in source (俺たち、ゾーンに入ったんじゃ！？) and contains the lowercase j the game font lacks a native-size glyph for (docs/CHANGELOG.md, docs/INTERMISSION_014.md); dropping it loses no meaning.
Reworded to avoid the same unsupported lowercase j; 'that's not...' preserves the source's repeated trailing-off protest/disbelief (そんなの……そんなの……！) at least as well as 'that's just...'.

checked_decisions.finding: Speaker of 'Is a thing like that truly necessary for the world you want?' genuinely cannot be pinned to Dewey vs. a subordinate from this context; translator's decision to leave it unassigned agreed.

'クダンの限界' -> 'Limit of Questions' is an established corpus term (first locked at batch_05943/proposals in batch_07926_glossary_proposals.json), correctly reused here and consistently in dialogue_10536 and again across the batch boundary at dialogue_10559/10584/10589/10600/10603 in batch_10537.

'that girl'/'that rider' kept literal rather than assumed to be Eureka. Agreed as the safer call: dialogue_10493-10496 foreshadow that what Renton/Nirvash is sensing may in fact be Anemone (revealed at dialogue_10497, next batch), so committing to 'Eureka' here would likely have been wrong.

'言えるよ！' rendered 'You can say it!' (addressed to Eureka rather than Eureka's own 'I can say it!'). Checked against the surrounding call-and-response: dialogue_10516 has Renton questioning Nirvash, and dialogue_10520-10521 ('It's okay to live... nobody ever said you're not allowed to') is a second line of reassurance to Eureka after her guilt at dialogue_10519 ('I wish I'd never noticed... this feeling'). Read as one consistent encouraging voice across 10517 and 10520-10521, 'You can say it!' is the better-supported reading; kept as is.
'コンパク' -> 'Compac' matches the established Eureka Seven term (Compac Drive); accurate, not previously in the four named glossary files but not a meaning defect.

uncertainties.issue: Speaker not settled (subordinate questioning Dewey vs. Dewey's own rhetorical aside). Ruling: translator's non-committal rendering is correct; genuinely cannot be resolved from this context.
Masculine 'boku' pronoun distinct from adjacent 'ore'/'watashi' lines; speaker not identified. Ruling: agree, cannot be settled from available context.

'that girl'/'that rider' referent (Eureka vs. Anemone). Ruling: agree with keeping it literal; later rows in this same batch suggest the referent may be Anemone, not Eureka, so committing to a name would likely have been an error.

Poetic monologue possibly echoing an insert song. Ruling: translation reads as an independent, faithful rendering of the Japanese wording and is consistent with Eureka's established voice/relationship to Renton; no fix needed.

'Ultimate' (katakana loanword) capitalized as a named power level; no glossary lock exists. Note: no batch_10457_glossary_proposals.json file was found for this batch even though the batch's own validation.terms references 'See glossary proposal' -- the proposal write-up appears to be one of the artifacts lost to the reported rate-limit interruption. Flagging for the orchestrator to have this term (and 'Compac', 'Kute-class') added to a glossary proposals file; not a meaning defect in the rows themselves.
